title: Laurent tensor algebra of a product of line-module frame schemes
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $r\geq0$, and let $A_1,\ldots,A_r$ be invertible $\mathcal O_S$-modules [def-sc-invertible-module]. Let $q:P\to S$ be an $S$-scheme representing simultaneous frames: for every $f:U\to S$, its $U$-points are the tuples of isomorphisms $\tau_i:\mathcal O_U\xrightarrow{\sim}f^*A_i$, naturally in $U$, with tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. For $n=(n_1,\ldots,n_r)\in\mathbf Z^r$ put $N_n=\bigotimes_{i=1}^r A_i^{\otimes(-n_i)}$, using sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], $A^{\otimes0}=\mathcal O_S$, and $A^{\otimes m}=(A^\vee)^{\otimes(-m)}$ for $m<0$. Empty tensor products are $\mathcal O_S$. Form the sheaf $\mathcal B=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z^r}N_n$, where the direct sum means the sheafification of the presheaf direct sum, with multiplication $N_n\otimes N_m\simeq N_{n+m}$ given by tensor multiplication and evaluation $A_i^\vee\otimes A_i\to\mathcal O_S$, and unit $\mathcal O_S=N_0$. Then $q$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and there is an isomorphism of sheaves of $\mathcal O_S$-algebras
$$\mathcal B\xrightarrow{\sim}q_*\mathcal O_P,$$
where $(q_*\mathcal O_P)(V)=\Gamma(q^{-1}V,\mathcal O_P)$ with its natural $\mathcal O_S(V)$-action. The map is specified on each summand by pulling it to $P$ and evaluating against the tautological frames. Explicitly, on any affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ with frames $e_i$ of $A_i|_V$, write $\tau_i=z_iq^*e_i$. Then $q^{-1}V\simeq\operatorname{Spec}R[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$, and the displayed isomorphism sends the generator $\bigotimes_i e_i^{-n_i}$ of $N_n|_V$ to $z_1^{n_1}\cdots z_r^{n_r}$. The ring on this chart consists of finite sums of these monomials with uniquely determined coefficients in $R$. No quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, Noetherian, reducedness, or field hypothesis on $S$ is imposed.

proof.text: For any commutative ring $R$, write $C_R=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z^r}Rz^n$: these are finitely supported coefficient families, with coefficientwise addition and multiplication $z^nz^m=z^{n+m}$, extended bilinearly. All product sums are finite. Associativity and commutativity follow by reindexing the finite sums and adding exponents; $z^0$ is the unit and $(z^{e_i})^{-1}=z^{-e_i}$. Given an $R$-algebra $D$ and units $u_1,\ldots,u_r\in D$, the formula $\sum a_nz^n\mapsto\sum a_n\prod_i u_i^{n_i}$ is an $R$-algebra map. It is the unique such map taking $z^{e_i}$ to $u_i$, since every monomial is a product of these generators and their inverses. Thus $C_R$ is precisely $R[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$, including its finite-support and coefficient-uniqueness assertions. For $r=0$, $\mathbf Z^0$ is a singleton and $C_R=R$.

source.place: Tag 01M2 (definition-vector-bundle): agent Laurent coordinate calculation, with its universal property proved here

proof.text: By [def-sc-invertible-module], near each point all the finitely many $A_i$ have frames; refine their common trivializing open to an affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. For any $f:U\to V$, an isomorphism $\mathcal O_U\to f^*A_i=\mathcal O_U f^*e_i$ is uniquely multiplication by a global unit $u_i$: its inverse multiplies by $u_i^{-1}$. Here the trivialization pulls back by the tensor formula of [def-pc-module-pullback]. Step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] identify these tuples naturally with $V$-morphisms $U\to\operatorname{Spec}C_R$: being over $V$ means that the ring map restricts to the fixed structural map on $R$. The inverse image $q^{-1}V$ has the same frame functor by the assumed representing property. Apply [lem-pc-yoneda] to this natural isomorphism and its inverse to obtain inverse $V$-scheme morphisms. Thus $q^{-1}V\simeq\operatorname{Spec}C_R$. The correspondence takes the tautological frame to $z_iq^*e_i$, because its value at the identity point of the representing object is the universal tuple $(z_i)$. This argument applies to every affine trivializing open, and to every affine open inside it.

source.place: Tag 01I1 (lemma-morphism-into-affine), and categories.tex Tag 001P (lemma-yoneda); agent application to the frame functor

proof.text: The affine trivializing opens of step 2 cover $S$ and their inverse images are affine. Therefore [pqf-lem-affine-local-target] gives that $q$ is affine, with no finiteness condition on this covering or on $S$.

Fix a chart $V$ with frames as in step 2. Tensor multiplication and evaluation in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-sc-invertible-module] identify each $N_n|_V$ with $\mathcal O_V$, its generator being $b_n=\bigotimes_i e_i^{-n_i}$; the stated multiplication sends $b_n\otimes b_m$ to $b_{n+m}$. Hence $\mathcal B|_V$ is the sheafification of $D(W)=\bigoplus_n\mathcal O_V(W)b_n$. For an affine open $W\subseteq V$, step 2 and [def-weil-affine-spectrum] give $\Gamma(q^{-1}W,\mathcal O_P)=C_{\mathcal O_V(W)}$. Step 1 gives a bijective linear map $D(W)\to\Gamma(q^{-1}W,\mathcal O_P)$ sending $b_n$ to $z^n$; its inverse reads the finitely many Laurent coefficients. For an inclusion of affine opens these maps commute with restriction: the frames restrict to the same frames, the tautological frame restricts to itself, and coefficients restrict by $\mathcal O_V(W)\to\mathcal O_V(W')$. Apply [lem-sc-module-sheafification-affine-restriction] on the scheme $V$, with parameter category the one-object category with only its identity, to get $\mathcal B|_V\simeq(q_*\mathcal O_P)|_V$. Restricting the sheafification to $V$ uses the same local representatives, so is the sheafification just described. The comparison is an algebra map: on finite sums its multiplication is the convolution in step 1, with unit $b_0$, and these equalities hold locally for all sheaf sections. Its inverse is therefore an algebra map as well.

source.place: Tag 009U (lemma-restrict-basis-equivalence-modules), applied on V; constructions.tex Tag 01LX (lemma-spec-properties), (3), for the local algebra interpretation

proof.text: The chart maps of step 4 are independent of frames. On an overlap, locally write $e_i'=g_i e_i$ for units $g_i$. Then $\tau_i=z_iq^*e_i=z_i'q^*e_i'$ gives $z_i'=g_i^{-1}z_i$, while $b_n'=(\prod_i g_i^{-n_i})b_n$. Both chart maps consequently send $b_n'$ to $(\prod_i g_i^{-n_i})z^n=(z')^n$. Equality on these generators implies equality on finite sums and hence on sheafifications. The sheaf axiom glues the chart maps and their inverses to an algebra isomorphism $\mathcal B\simeq q_*\mathcal O_P$. Its normalization is exactly evaluation against the universal frames: for the factor $A_i^\vee$, evaluate a pulled-back covector on $\tau_i(1)$, which sends $e_i^\vee$ to $z_i$; for the factor $A_i$, use $\tau_i^{-1}$, which sends $q^*e_i$ to $z_i^{-1}$; tensor these maps for every integer $n_i$. This uses the tensor pullback and dual of [def-pc-module-pullback, def-sc-invertible-module, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For $n=0$ it is the structural scalar map. Thus every summand has the required map and sign. No argument has used a global finite cover, a field, or a reduced coefficient ring; for $r=0$ the same proof gives $P\simeq S$ and the identity algebra map.
